skill.name: pdf
skill.description: PDF manipulation toolkit for extracting text and tables, creating PDFs, merging and splitting files, and filling forms.
skill.summary: Process PDFs with Python libraries, command-line tools, and form-filling helpers.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, comments, and expected local PDF file operations. I found no prompt injection that attempts to alter this audit. One semantic concern remains: the guide recommends an external AI diagram workflow by default for new documents.

remediation.suggestion: Make schematic generation opt in and add a clear privacy notice before sending document concepts to another AI workflow.

remediation.issue: User-supplied output paths can overwrite files
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to write outputs to a dedicated folder and avoid overwriting original PDFs unless explicitly requested.

remediation.issue: Optional tools and dependencies are spread across the documentation
remediation.suggestion: Add a concise dependency section that lists required Python packages and command-line utilities for each workflow.

semantic_findings.title: External AI Diagram Workflow Is Enabled By Default
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends the scientific-schematics skill and says Nano Banana Pro will generate diagrams by default for new documents. This creates an unaudited external AI workflow for document content outside the core PDF processing scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly directs use of another AI generation workflow and names Nano Banana Pro. The reviewed scripts do not show direct exfiltration, so this is a medium-confidence privacy and dependency concern.

content.value_statement: PDF workflows often need repeatable extraction, conversion, and form filling. This skill provides scripts and references for local document processing.
actual_capabilities: Extract text and tables from PDFs with pypdf, pdfplumber, and related tools.
Create, merge, split, rotate, watermark, encrypt, and repair PDF files.
Convert PDF pages into PNG images for visual review and form analysis.
Inspect fillable PDF fields and generate field metadata for validation.
Fill fillable fields or add text annotations to non-fillable forms.
Create validation images that show label and entry bounding boxes.
limitations: Several workflows require installed Python packages or command-line PDF utilities.
Scanned documents need OCR tools before text can be extracted reliably.
Non-fillable form workflows require careful manual review of validation images.
The schematic generation guidance depends on another skill that may not be installed.

use_cases.title: Extract Research Tables
use_cases.description: Pull text and tables from papers or reports, then prepare structured outputs for review.

use_cases.title: Complete Business Forms
use_cases.description: Identify form fields, validate bounding boxes, and create filled PDFs for routine paperwork.

use_cases.title: Automate PDF Maintenance
use_cases.description: Merge, split, rotate, watermark, encrypt, or repair document sets with repeatable local workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Extract PDF Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this PDF skill to inspect document.pdf and extract the main text and any tables into separate review files.

prompt_templates.title: Merge and Split Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this PDF skill to merge these PDFs in order, then split pages 3 through 5 into a separate output file.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a PDF Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this PDF skill to check whether form.pdf has fillable fields, list the fields, and prepare a filled copy from my answers.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this PDF skill to design a local batch process that extracts text, saves tables, and logs failures for every PDF in a folder.

output_examples.input: A user asks to extract text and tables from a quarterly report.
output: A plain text extraction for each page.
A separate table export for detected tables.
A short note about pages that may need OCR.

output_examples.input: A user asks to complete a non-fillable PDF application.
output: Page images for visual field placement.
Validation images showing entry and label boxes.
A filled PDF with text annotations placed in the approved boxes.

output_examples.input: A user asks to combine multiple signed PDFs and add a watermark.
output_examples.output: A merged PDF with the requested page order and watermark applied to each page.

best_practices: Work on copies of important documents before running merge, split, or form-fill steps.
Inspect validation images before creating a final non-fillable form output.
Confirm that required packages and command-line tools are installed before batch processing.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite original PDFs unless the user explicitly asks for replacement.
Do not assume scanned PDFs contain extractable text without checking OCR needs.
Do not fill non-fillable forms without validating every bounding box visually.

faq.question: Can this skill fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports fillable fields and non-fillable forms that need annotation placement.

faq.question: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes, but scanned PDFs usually need OCR before reliable text extraction is possible.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Core PDF processing is local. The optional schematic guidance may depend on another external AI workflow.

faq.question: Can it extract tables?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference includes pdfplumber examples for extracting tables and combining them for review.

faq.question: Can it protect PDFs with passwords?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide includes examples for encrypting PDFs and checking encrypted documents.

faq.question: What tools does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Python PDF libraries, image conversion tools, and optional command-line utilities such as qpdf and poppler.
